attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: A present-tense description of venture behaviour as of August 2023. The normalised version keeps 'AI and very little else' and the framing clause. The drafter correctly classed it as an observation.

contract.note: He named no measure. The plain reading uses venture money and interest from January 2023 to the post date, and treats 'very little else' as strong but not literally zero. That is an ordinary reading. Because he gave no measure, a reading based only on enthusiasm could change the result.

evidence.note: Crunchbase report on H1 2023, dated before the post. It singles out AI fervour as the standout force while overall funding fell. This supports Part A.
Crunchbase: AI took 18% of global H1 2023 funding, including the $10B OpenAI round. Most money went to non-AI companies, which cuts against 'very little else'.

Crunchbase July 2023 recap, published two days before the post. AI got about 11%, behind health care, renewable energy and fintech, and the recap says AI did not stand out. This meets the contradiction condition.
Large Q2 2023 rounds went to companies outside AI (Shein, 1Komma5°, Northvolt). This is modest extra evidence against 'very little else'.
PitchBook full-year 2023 US data (AI about one third of dollars). It covers months after the post and only the US, so it is context only.

reviews.rationale: Part A holds: Crunchbase singles out AI as the standout of 2023 venture funding (e1). Part B fails: AI was 18% of H1 funding (e2) and 11% in July, behind three other sectors (e3). Most venture money went to non-AI companies, which meets the contract's contradiction condition for 'very little else'. AI enthusiasm was real, but it was not near-exclusive.
